transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-15
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Marcus Li (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Elmbridge Head of ML), Daniel Park (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Aisha Khan (FinOps)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Quarterly health & cost check; spike risk during marketing promo; plan for Dedicated pilot and further benchmarks; action items captured.

00:00 Marcus Li: hey everyone, thanks for joining, do you all see my screen?
00:07 Sofia Martinez: yep, good to go, thanks Marcus
00:10 Marcus Li: cool, quick agenda — usage recap, cost drivers, reliability, then propose next steps. Priya will share the stress test plan.
00:23 Daniel Park: quick note, we had a pretty nasty latency tail last week during the flash sale, 95th was ok but 99th spiked to 2.1s per token which blew our page load SLO.
00:36 Priya Kapoor: yeah we pulled logs, looks like KV cache misses coincided with an unusual token length distribution — some requests hit longer contexts, so cache warming didn't help.
00:47 Liam O'Connor: just to confirm, are you talking about the Redwood runtime cache or our redis prefix cache? sometimes the terminology gets mixed up in the logs.
00:55 Priya Kapoor: good call — initial read was Redwood's KV cache (the model-side cache), but we also saw our middleware replays. logs in the deck link (shared deck: https://redwood-hosted/decks/elmbridge-may15)
01:08 Marcus Li: ok, for context Elmbridge saw a 3x spike for embeddings requests during the week-long promo; embeddings were the primary cost driver. Marcus: quick question to Aisha, is the embeddings pipeline batched or per-request?
01:23 Aisha Khan: currently it's mostly per-request for freshness, we do micro-batches sometimes but not consistently. FinOps is feeling the cost — impressions are driving a lot of small embed calls.
01:36 Marcus Li: right, that's a classic cost/latency tradeoff. you can batch many small embed calls on Redwood Hosted to drop per-unit cost but latency increases slightly. Priya, can you outline the batching quant recommendations?
01:48 Priya Kapoor: sure — preliminary notes: group by model and input length, prefer a 200ms batching window for most user flows, switch to async batch for non-blocking analytics. also recommend 8-bit quant for the heavy embed-only endpoint, should be safe for Elmbridge's similarity scores.
02:05 Daniel Park: hmm the quantization angle worries our QA team — they saw small drift in similarity ranking in a separate eval. how do we guard against quality regressions?
02:17 Priya Kapoor: we run evaluation harnesses with your dev prompts — Redwood Optimize suggestions include a canary rollout: 10% of requests with quant model, monitor precision@10 and rerun prompt set daily. if regression > 2% rollback automatically.
02:34 Sofia Martinez: that canary sounds good. what's the typical rollback window?
02:38 Priya Kapoor: most rollbacks are automated within 5-10 minutes if the monitor triggers, manual review for the post-mortem.
02:45 Marcus Li: switching to capacity — we recommended Dedicated reserved for predictable peak throughput; that gives you pre-warmed pools and lower per-token, but you pay baseline for the reservation. for flash promos we can enable burst capacity back to hosted for overflow.
03:01 Aisha Khan: can you quantify cost delta? last month we used 2M embed units, cost was, uh, we got a bill that surprised finance.
03:10 Marcus Li: we'll send a detailed scenario set but rule-of-thumb: hosted per-embed unit X, dedicated baseline reduces unit cost by around 20-35% depending on utilization; reserved commitment and burst premiums apply. I'll put specific numbers in the follow-up.
03:24 Daniel Park: also need to talk SLA — we saw a multi-region failover lag. Is Redwood's routing multi-region for Hosted?
03:32 Priya Kapoor: yes, Hosted routes by region and will fallback to next available region, but that can add latency. For strict latency SLOs, Dedicated in-region is better. Private/VPC options available if you need data residency.
03:45 Liam O'Connor: about security: we need SOC2 artifact pack and SAML SSO integration timeline — our security team triages next week.
03:53 Marcus Li: we have a SOC2 package, I'll attach the audit binder. SSO is supported via SAML and SCIM provisioning; typical integration timeline is 2-3 weeks with Elmbridge's IdP.
04:05 Sofia Martinez: great. one other ask: can we get per-route token breakdown? the console shows aggregate but we need to map to product features.
04:13 Marcus Li: yes, token-level routing and per-route dashboards exist, we'll export a per-route CSV for your product metrics.
04:20 Priya Kapoor: on reliability testing plan — I'm proposing a 48-hour stress benchmark: synthetic traffic shaped to your histogram, include bursty 10s spikes, verify 95/99 latency, error rates, and KV-cache warmup effects.
04:33 Daniel Park: that'll be helpful. include a run with fallback to Hosted while Dedicated is saturated, we want to see real fallback latencies.
04:42 Priya Kapoor: absolutely. I'll add a test variant with Dedicated in-region saturated and Hosted fallback.
04:48 Aisha Khan: timeline? we need results before next week's finance review.
04:52 Priya Kapoor: aiming to run tests by Wed 2025-05-21 and share preliminary results by Thursday.
04:58 Marcus Li: quick note on model transparency — you mentioned drift and quality. Redwood can pin model versions and provide traceable rollouts; our evals can be attached to each rollout so you can audit quality over time.
05:12 Sofia Martinez: that helps. also curious about embedding vector storage — are you recommending third-party vs Redwood-managed cache?
05:20 Priya Kapoor: for similarity pipelines we recommend external vector store for long-term persistence, Redwood can cache recent vectors for inference to speed up cold-starts. we saw in your logs many redundant embed calls where a local cache could have avoided extra compute.
05:36 Daniel Park: yeah we've been iterating on our cache TTLs. there may be a quick win there to reduce billable units.
05:44 Marcus Li: agreed. next steps recap: Priya runs stress tests; Marcus sends pricing scenarios and SOC2 bundle; Elmbridge to share traffic histograms. then we reconvene for exec QBR.
05:56 Sofia Martinez: one more thing — competitor angle: our infra team is considering an in-house GPU cluster for embeddings, tradeoff being control vs ops cost. any notes you can share on break-even?
06:07 Marcus Li: we'll model three scenarios: fully in-house, hosted, and hybrid with Dedicated + on-prem for embeddings. include TCO over 12/24 months.
06:18 Daniel Park: perfect. ok that's it from my side. thanks everyone.
06:22 Marcus Li: thanks — we'll follow up with the items by next week.

End of transcript.
